name: Furniture and mattresses
note: CBP generally determines the country of origin for furniture and mattresses based on where the primary structural components, such as tabletops, metal cabinets, or foam mattress cores, are fabricated from raw or semi-finished materials. Conversely, simple assembly, co-packaging pre-made bases with tops, attaching electronic controllers, or placing finished mattresses into sofa frames does not constitute a substantial transformation. Tables sold unassembled took the origin of their stone tops, not of the welded, painted bases packed with them (version 2). Upholstery can decide: cutting and sewing covers onto frames built with their springs, foam and padding made the seat a product of the country that built the frame and upholstered it, while fitting covers to finished foreign frames did not; assembling finished, stained cabinet kits into cabinets and machining, staining and lacquering rough-cut wood into a headboard also conferred origin (version 3). No ruling found turns on finishing alone. Written from 15 CBP substantial-transformation rulings outside the dev and held-out splits (D138), with one table ruling from the train pool added in version 2 (D782) and seven older rulings fetched by number from CROSS, kept in the cited-only pool, added in version 3 (D862); every cited ruling was checked against its facts and holding. Costs are illustrative defaults; users edit them.

groups.name: Tabletop and panels
operations: press laminate or wood veneer sheets onto particleboard or MDF substrate
precision cut panels to shape and apply hot melt glue edge banding
mold, cast, and finish engineered stone or quartz tabletops from stone powder and resin

precedent.note: CBP often finds that fabricating the tabletop imparts the essential character and origin of a table (H330862, H338728, N339685), including cutting, bevelling and polishing engineered quartz slabs into tops for tables sold unassembled (N334531), though importing pre-cut laminated MDF boards for complex desk assembly did not control origin (N344246).

groups.name: Frame and base
operations: stamp, shear, laser cut, pierce, and bend steel coil or metal tubing into structural plates, legs, and rails
extrude and shape aluminum rails, posts, and blind slats
weld metal legs, frames, and cabinet bodies and apply powder coating
cut, mold, join, and stain wood pedestal bases and structural legs
sand, mortise, tenon and drill rough-cut wood into posts, rails and cabinet parts, then stain, lacquer or seal them

precedent.note: Stamping, extruding, and welding metal into structural bodies or frames confers origin when it forms the core structure (H330862, N335242, N338514), whereas manufacturing a wood pedestal alone did not confer origin compared to the stone tabletop (N339685), nor did welding and painting metal bases or machining and painting wood bases in China for tables with Thai stone tops (N334531). Turning rough-cut Chinese wood into headboard posts and rails in Taiwan by sanding, mortising, tenoning, staining and lacquering made the headboard Taiwanese (N228696), and cutting, engraving, drilling, staining and sealing wood into kitchen cabinets in Mexico made them Mexican (N322258).

groups.name: Foam and upholstery
operations: extrude, layer, and cut polyurethane memory foam to size
cut and sew textile fabrics, fireproof socks, welt cords, and zippered outer covers
enclose foam layers and innerspring coils into sewn fireproof socks and zippered textile covers
cut fabric to pattern and sew it into upholstery covers, then stretch, staple and sew the covers onto frames fitted with their springs, foam and padding

precedent.note: Extruding, layering, and cutting memory foam and zipping it into covers in Japan established Japanese origin for the mattresses even after they were placed into sleeper sofas in another country (N348576, N339107, N339646). Pouring, curing and cutting foam and covering it in Vietnam made a foam mattress Vietnamese despite Chinese covers (N307432). Sewing covers cut abroad onto U.S.-built frames with their springs, foam and padding made the seats U.S. products, though fitting the same covers to finished foreign frames would be simple assembly (N101033); fitted covers cut in China to fit U.S. sofa and chair frames were Chinese as covers and lost that identity once fitted (N064195).

groups.name: Controls and mechanisms
operations: populate printed circuit board assemblies for motion, sound, Bluetooth, and height control
assemble mechanical lift, scissor, and cordless spring mechanisms with motors and actuators
manufacture digital hand controllers, power hubs, and electric firebox displays

precedent.note: Populating the main control PCB and assembling the motorized scissor mechanism contributed to origin (N330057), whereas supplying imported hand controllers and control boxes did not confer origin (H330862). Building a mechanically adjustable bed foundation, with its articulating electromechanical structure, in Vietnam from mostly Chinese parts made it Vietnamese (N306524).

groups.name: Final assembly
operations: mount controllers, brackets, latches, drawers, and hardware onto tabletops, frames, or cabinets
unroll and place finished foam mattresses onto sleeper sofa or ottoman frames
combine and package finished tabletops with pedestals, legs, or bases for retail shipment
pack tabletops with unassembled bases and hardware as knock-down kits for assembly by the buyer
assemble imported kits of finished, stained cabinet parts into complete cabinets

precedent.note: Final assembly confers origin when paired with substantial component fabrication or complex multi-part integration (N338514, N344246), but merely co-packaging or minor joining does not transform the components (N334531, N348576, N339107, N339646). Assembling kits of finished, stained and topcoated Chinese face frames, doors and boxes into kitchen and bath cabinets in the United States made them U.S. products (N087858).
